name: file-upload
purpose: File picker built on a native <input type="file"> opened by a real button, with an optional drag-and-drop zone around it (never the only way in). Validates MIME type and extension (both when both are configured), per-file size, total size, and file count; files that break a rule are not added and the reason is shown and announced. A FormControl whose value is File[]. It never reads file contents and never performs network requests.
whenToUse: Attaching one or more files to a form.
Feeding an Upload Queue that transfers files as soon as they are chosen.
Any file selection that needs consistent, localized validation messages.
whenNotToUse: Choosing a folder tree or very large batches (thousands of files): use a dedicated tool.
Capturing photos or media in-page: use native capture APIs.
As a security control: client-side type checks can be bypassed; validate on the server.
responsive: Full width of its container. The drop zone content wraps and centers; file rows wrap the size and reason under the name; remove buttons keep a 24 px target.
rtl: Logical properties throughout: icons and remove buttons follow the inline direction. File names are rendered as text in their own direction.
theme: Dashed color-border-strong zone on color-surface; drag-over uses color-selected with color-selected-text; errors use color-error-fg. Forced-colors mode uses CanvasText borders and a Highlight drag-over border.
security: File names, reasons, and messages are rendered with textContent (never HTML). MIME types come from the browser (usually derived from the file name) and are not proof of content: always validate type and size on the server (for example by magic bytes). The accept attribute is only a hint; every file is re-checked. No file contents are read. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: Files stay in memory as File objects and in the native input (for native form submission). Nothing is persisted, logged, or transmitted; uploading is the application's (or Upload Queue's consumer transport's) job.

performance.testedScale: 200 files in one selection in the performance test; tested with 500 fields on a page.

limitations: Sizes use decimal units (1 kB = 1,000 bytes), as Intl formats them.
Duplicate detection uses name, size, and modification time.
Dropped folders are rejected; folder upload (webkitdirectory) is not supported.
The drag-over highlight depends on the browser exposing "Files" in dataTransfer.types during dragenter.
Without a DataTransfer constructor (very old browsers) the native input cannot be synchronized; getFormValue() stays authoritative.
Manual screen-reader verification (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) is pending.
unsupported: Reading, previewing, or transforming file contents (use Upload Queue previews for images).
Rendering HTML in labels, hints, or file names.
antiPatterns: Making the drop zone the only way to choose files.
Trusting the browser MIME type or the accept attribute as a security check.
Showing raw server error text for rejected uploads.

adapters.angular: @absoluteui/angular/file-upload: AuiFileUpload directive ([auiFileUpload]) with ControlValueAccessor (File[]) and Validator.
adapters.react: @absoluteui/react/file-upload: AuiFileUpload component; controlled (value/defaultValue + onValueChange) or uncontrolled.
